to_reason: [2 direction; 3 test] The note's chronology runs backwards. DERIVED_FROM asks which-came-first by independent historical reasoning (Law 7): the finite N-point sum D[k]=sum x[n]e^(-2piikn/N) is the older object — Gauss applied finite discrete cosine sums to asteroid-orbit determination in 1805 (published 1809, Theoria Motus), and the same finite-sum transform recurs in early 19th-century work on finite data. The DTFT as a named formal object — the bilateral sum over all integers x[n]e^(-jwn) yielding a continuous 2pi-periodic function of real frequency — belongs to the digital-filter era (Zadeh and Chertkov 1959; Rabiner and Gold 1975; Oppenheim and Schafer), where discrete-time sequences became the standard input. The note's premise 'the continuous-frequency analysis of discrete sequences predates the finite-grid DFT' is not supported by the record. The true mathematical relation — DFT equals DTFT evaluated at w=2pi k/N, as the target's own definition states — is a special-case/generalization relation, not historical derivation; if anything the continuous object is the generalization of the finite sum, which points the other way. Direction and historical test both fail.
